title: MedAgent-Pro: Towards Evidence-based Multi-modal Medical Diagnosis via Reasoning Agentic Workflow
one_liner: MedAgent-Pro separates diagnosis into a guideline-based plan and a patient-specific evidence loop, so each conclusion is tied to retrieved clinical guidance and measured findings from the patient data.
lead: A usable diagnostic system cannot stop at naming a disease. It must show which findings support the conclusion, which guideline step justified the next test, and what evidence ruled out alternatives. MedAgent-Pro builds that structure explicitly. One stage retrieves disease-level guidance and turns it into a diagnostic plan. A second stage runs patient-level reasoning: it calls visual and analytic tools on scans, reports, and other patient data, stores the findings in memory, and reflects on whether the current conclusion is actually supported. The goal is not only a correct label but a trace of why that label was chosen.

problem.h2: Why direct multimodal diagnosis is not enough
paras: Modern diagnosis uses multiple data sources at once: images, symptoms, laboratory values, history, and clinical guidelines. A direct answer from a vision-language model compresses all of that into one step. That is risky because the system may skip a missing lab value, ignore a contradictory image finding, or jump to a familiar disease without checking guideline order.

Clinical use needs evidence that can be inspected. A doctor must be able to ask: which image region suggested pneumonia, which lab value supported infection, and which guideline branch recommended this test next? If the model cannot answer those questions, the final diagnosis is hard to trust even when it happens to be correct.

The paper addresses this by splitting diagnosis into a standard plan and a personalized execution loop. This helps because the standard plan enforces disease-specific steps, while the execution loop checks the actual patient record against those steps before producing a conclusion.

callout.html: Retrieve disease guidelines first, turn them into an explicit diagnostic plan, then let a patient-level agent gather findings step by step and revise its memory whenever the evidence does not support the current conclusion.

steps.text: A retrieval-augmented stage searches medical guidelines and reference material relevant to the suspected disease area.
The system turns the retrieved guidance into an ordered checklist: which findings to inspect, which tests matter, and which alternatives must be ruled out.

steps.b: Analyze the patient data with tools
steps.text: A patient-level agent calls visual models and other analytic tools on scans, reports, and structured values to gather concrete findings.
After each step, the agent checks whether the current memory contains enough evidence for the working diagnosis. If not, it revises the plan or asks for another action.

steps.b: Emit a diagnosis plus evidence trace
steps.text: The final output ties each conclusion to the findings and guideline steps that support it.

paras: The paper changes diagnosis from one-shot prediction into a controlled workflow with two levels of reasoning. The disease level defines what should be checked in general for a condition class. The patient level decides how to check those items on this patient. That separation matters because it prevents patient-specific noise from rewriting clinical procedure, while still allowing the agent to adapt the next action to the evidence already collected.

hidden.h2: The hidden quantity: evidence support coverage
hidden.name: How much of the conclusion is backed by explicit findings
paras: The important quantity is support coverage: for each major claim in the diagnosis, how much direct evidence is already present in memory? A diagnosis is weak when the conclusion is stated but one of its required findings is absent, contradictory, or only implied. It is strong when each key claim points to a measured lab value, an image finding, or a retrieved guideline condition.

Reflection uses this quantity to decide whether to stop or keep investigating. If support coverage is low, the agent should not finalize because the conclusion still rests on gaps. If support coverage is high, the final answer is easier to inspect because each step has a concrete backing item.

heat.caption: Darker means a claim has stronger support from explicit findings. Outlined cells mark states where the case can be finalized.

reads.html: A diagnosis is only ready when the important claims are linked to actual findings rather than a fluent summary.
MedAgent-Pro uses evidence-based reflection to inspect memory and adjust the patient-level reasoning process until the current conclusion is backed by sufficient clinical evidence.

mechanism.h2: Why the two-level agent is useful
paras: The disease-level plan reduces omission errors. Without it, the system may ignore a key exclusion criterion simply because it is not salient in the current prompt. The retrieved plan keeps those checks visible, so the patient-level agent is repeatedly compared against a standard clinical sequence.

The patient-level loop reduces unsupported conclusions. Tool outputs turn images and numbers into explicit findings, memory stores those findings in a reusable form, and reflection asks whether the evidence base is complete enough for the current diagnosis. This works by forcing the model to convert raw multimodal input into inspected intermediate facts before it commits to a final decision.

stages.s: Patient case and suspected disease area

math.words: Finalize only when the accumulated evidence covers the required diagnostic findings and keeps contradictions low.
math.equation: Support(d) = sum_k w_k * Evidence_k - sum_m u_m * Missing_m, finalize if Support(d) >= tau
symbols: an observed finding that supports requirement k
a missing or contradictory item for requirement m
penalty weight for missing or contradictory evidence
minimum support score needed before finalizing

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose pneumonia requires three major supports: image opacity, fever, and raised inflammatory marker.
The agent finds opacity on the scan and elevated marker in the lab panel, but fever is absent.
If the first two supports each contribute 1 point and the missing fever contributes a penalty of 1 point, the current support score is 1 + 1 - 1 = 1.
If the threshold tau is 2, the case cannot be finalized yet. The agent must collect more evidence or reconsider the diagnosis.
After history review reveals measured fever, the score becomes 1 + 1 + 1 = 3, so the diagnosis can now be finalized.

math.note: The exact score can vary across diseases. The important idea is that a diagnosis should be blocked until its required evidence is present.

charts.title: One-shot diagnosis
charts.note: The system can still be right, but the user has little visibility into which clinical checks were skipped.

charts.title: MedAgent-Pro
charts.note: The workflow improves inspectability because each patient-level step is compared against a retrieved diagnostic plan.

items.b: Retrieved guidance is incomplete or outdated.
items.html: If retrieval misses the relevant guideline section, the standardized plan starts from a weak base and later reflection can only partially repair that error.
Patient-level reasoning depends on image analyzers and other measurement tools. A wrong intermediate finding can propagate because later steps treat it as evidence.
If the reflection step only asks whether the diagnosis sounds plausible, it will accept fluent summaries. It must check whether each required claim points to stored evidence.
Keep the disease-level plan explicit, log every tool result into memory, and make the reflection prompt ask for missing findings and rule-out gaps before allowing a final answer.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a diagnostic sandbox with multimodal cases that include images, short clinical notes, and lab tables. Compare a direct multimodal baseline against MedAgent-Pro. For each case, record the retrieved plan, the sequence of tool actions, the final diagnosis, and the list of supporting findings that can be traced back to the input.
demo.metric_eq: Diagnosis accuracy, evidence support coverage, and rate of unsupported final claims
demo.closing: The demo should show that the main gain is not only a better label. The stronger result is that the final diagnosis is easier to inspect because each major claim is attached to a concrete finding and a guideline step.
